title: Rule file (rules.v1)
description: The rule-file schema of docs/rule-engine-spec.md section 6.2.3. This file states STRUCTURE only -- which keys exist, what type each holds, which keys a given action verb accepts. What an operand MEANS is the DSL compiler's job: $ref resolution, the $$ref escape, and the rejection of unrecognised $-prefixed keys all live in OperatorMaps, because section 6.2.3 requires those three judgements in one place.

apiVersion.description: Section 6.2.3: a file naming an unknown version is a compile error, not a best-effort parse.

quantifier.description: Section 2.5's quantifier, spelled as section 6.2.1 spells an operator: the camelCase of the constant. Absent means exists, which is what every pattern written before this key existed meant. Only implemented quantifiers are spellable -- accumulate is reserved in the enum and deferred by section 1, and admitting a spelling here would promise a shape the version that implements it may not want. A forAll pattern's joins choose which facts it is about; its own constraints are what is asserted of them.

condition.description: The CEL escape hatch of section 6.4. Accepted by this schema and rejected by the DSL compiler, so that the message names the feature and says where it arrives.

operatorMap.description: Section 6.2.1's table. Several operators in one map are AND-ed, the same way several fields in one where block are.

bound.description: A comparable literal, or an object -- which is either a $ref join operand or, escaped as $$ref, a literal object. Section 2.6.1 orders numbers and strings only, so a boolean or an array here is a rule that can never match.

between.description: Named bounds rather than positional, per section 2.5: a two-element array cannot express inclusivity without a convention that then has to be documented, validated and remembered. Both inclusivity flags default to true. Note what is deliberately NOT stated here: that a between needs at least one BOUND. This schema could say it, and would then catch { } while still missing { fromInclusive: true } -- so the DSL check has to exist regardless, and having both means the better message wins only half the time. OperatorMaps owns it, and raises empty-range for either shape.

action.description: Section 6.2.2's five verbs. Written as if/then per verb rather than a oneOf, because a oneOf failure reports only that nothing matched, and the author needs to know which key THIS verb was missing.

logical.description: Section 4.4's truth maintenance. When true the new fact is a CONCLUSION held up by the match that inserted it, and is withdrawn when that match stops holding -- the negated fact arrives, a forAll counterexample turns up, or a bound fact is retracted. Absent means false, which is what every insertFact written before this key existed meant. Only insertFact accepts it; on any other verb it is an unknown key.

payload.description: Field name to value. A value is a literal, a fire-time { $ref: alias.field }, or a { $expr: ... } expression of section 6.4; the DSL compiler tells them apart. Names may be dotted, and compile to nested paths the way a where-block field does.
